finding: §3.1's new sentence "Neither state arises through tp: `tp set --workflow checks=`, `tp set --workflow --project` and `tp validate` all run the validator over the whole slice and reject both an invalid entry and a duplicate class, so a workflow containing either was hand-edited" is false on two counts, and it is load-bearing: it is the sole justification for "tp adds no advisory for the condition". (a) `tp validate` does NOT reject — `validateConvergence` (internal/engine/validate.go:389-397) emits a Finding with Severity "warning" whose message is literally "invalid check entries are skipped at execution time", so `tp validate` exits 0 on a workflow holding an invalid entry or a duplicate class. Only `tp set --workflow` (internal/cli/set.go:360) and `tp set --workflow --project` (internal/cli/set_project.go:74) exit ExitValidation. A tester following this sentence writes an assertion that `tp validate` exits non-zero on such a fixture and it fails, and the "was hand-edited" premise cannot be asserted at all.

finding: The paragraph accepting that --quiet silences the missing-round advisory rests on a claim that is false in most reachable cases: "the payload reports the same condition structurally through spec_coverage_clean_rounds and an empty role_streaks". Test 6 pins the advisory but no test pins the structural claim, so the error survives implementation.

finding: The paragraph distinguishing `role_streaks` from `overlap_report` opens with "`tp audit --status` already emits `overlap_report`, which also has one entry per role". finding: The paragraph reconciling `divergence` with `engine.Converged` states: "a round that recorded zero rows, or whose file was later deleted, counts as clean for `engine.ConsecutiveClean` while ending every role's streak". The second half is wrong about the mechanism it cites. `engine.ConsecutiveClean` (internal/engine/reviewstate.go) walks the stored per-round `clean` boolean; deleting a round's NDJSON file does not touch that flag. A round recorded with findings and later stripped of its file still counts as NOT clean, so it ends the streaks *and* stops `ConsecutiveClean` — the asymmetry the paragraph is built on does not arise there. Only the zero-rows round (recorded `findings: 0` → `clean: true`) actually supports the sentence, together with a round recorded clean whose file was later deleted. §2.6 leans on the same claim by asserting the stored flag is untouched, so the mis-citation propagates into the release's central "the gate is untouched" argument.

The premise does not separate valid from invalid entries in the sink this release is built around. runMechanicalChecks is reached only from internal/cli/review.go:467 (bare prompt emission), internal/cli/review_status.go:67 (guarded by `if check`) and internal/cli/review_regression.go:95; tp review <spec> --record <file> — §3.2 mode 1, the mode that filters mechanize_candidates, the register-a-check hint and next_action — never executes any check, valid or not. So on the release's headline path a VALID entry is equally "never executed" yet mechanizes its class, and §3.2 states the opposite grounding two paragraphs later: "Whether the registered check passes is irrelevant: registration is the trigger." The rule itself is unambiguous; the reason given for it is not the reason that actually holds, which is the shape the earlier finding was accepted for.

finding: §3.2 item 1 specifies suppression separately for "the register-a-check `hint`" and "the class list handed to `next_action`", entrenching a duplication this release is otherwise well placed to remove. On `tp review --record` the two sinks emit the same instruction on the same payload: `hint` is the constant `write a mechanical check for each candidate class and register it: tp set --workflow checks='[...]'` (internal/cli/review_report.go:54, emitted whenever candidates are non-empty at review_record.go:169-171), while `next_action` branch 3 emits `register a check for the recurring %q class (tp set --workflow checks='[{"class":%q,"cmd":"…"}]'), then run the next review round: tp review <spec> --record <file>` (internal/engine/nextaction.go:42-46). The second strictly dominates the first — it names the class, the exact command with the class filled in, and the follow-on step — so `hint` adds roughly 110 bytes of no new information on every candidate-bearing round, in a payload that is not `--compact`-gated. §3.2's consequence 1 even ties them together ("that hint is already conditional on a non-empty list"), so the release is already reasoning about both as one directive.

finding: §4 requires both summary substrings in `skills/tp/SKILL.md`, and SKILL.md bytes are the most expensive bytes in this project: §4 itself notes it is "loaded into every agent context alongside CLAUDE.md", so the cost is paid in every session forever, not once per invocation. One of the two required strings, `audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row`, is a fragment of the `divergence.hint` constant that tp emits verbatim at the exact moment it becomes relevant (§2.6), and §4 already pins that same sentence verbatim in `REFERENCE.md` (sentence 5) and requires `CLAUDE.md` to carry the rule. After this release the sentence is maintained in five artifacts — the code constant, REFERENCE.md, README.md, SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md — and the SKILL.md copy is the only one whose cost is per-session-permanent. It also carries the least: an agent cannot act on the prose ahead of time, whereas what it does need in advance is the set of keys it must now parse (`spec_coverage_clean_rounds`, `role_streaks`, `divergence`, `mechanized_classes`) — none of which §4 requires SKILL.md to name.

finding: Test 8 says of the four `role_streaks == []` states: "The last two are the states that emit no advisory, so the field is the only disclosure." Three of the four emit no advisory. By §2.1 the advisory fires only for a round *in the walked segment* that contributes no rows, so "no recorded round exists at all" (state 1) emits nothing either — there is no round to name. Only state 2 (latest round's file deleted / `file` empty) emits it. The sentence as written tells an implementer that state 1 has an advisory to assert, which no §2.1 rule produces.
